message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom and was selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Key highlights of his career include:

- **NBA Championships**: Four titles (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) with the Heat and Lakers.
- **MVP Awards**: Four regular‑season MVPs (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and two Finals MVPs (2012, 2013).
- **All‑Star Appearances**: 19 selections (as of 2023), including multiple All‑NCAA and All‑World honors.
- **Scoring & Playmaking**: Known for his combination of size, athleticism, and skill, LeBron has averaged over 27 points per game throughout his career and is also a prolific passer.
- **Off‑Court Impact**: He is a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. His LeBron James Family Foundation focuses on education initiatives, notably the “I Promise School” in Akron. He has also produced films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment.

Beyond basketball, LeBron has become a cultural icon, influencing fashion, music, and social activism. He continues to play at a high level into his late thirties, maintaining his status as a dominant force in the NBA.
